title: Checkpoint 7: Animal Class Hierarchy
hints: Model the tree: Animal → Dog → Corgi/Poodle, Animal → Cat → Persian/Lion.
`Cat` needs `init(isTame:)` that sets `isTame` before calling `super.init(legs: 4)`; subclasses call it with fixed values.
Build `[Animal]` with a `switch` in `compactMap`, then map to `"\($0.speak()) (\($0.legs) legs)"`.
jsBridge: Class hierarchies with overrides and custom initialisers, as in JS `class Dog extends Animal`. Swift adds rules: designated initialisers, `super.init`, `override` and `final`. They feel heavy because Swift steers you towards protocols and structs.

compass.q: How many of Swift's class rules have no JS equivalent? Which one catches the most bugs?
Rewrite with a protocol `Animal` and structs. What do you lose? (Shared stored `legs`.)
Does `Poodle` inherit `Dog`'s initialisers automatically? When would it stop?
Why are deep class hierarchies rare in modern Swift apps?
